skill.name: router
skill.description: Routes development requests to appropriate Claude Code skills, agents, and slash commands using intent analysis and project context.
skill.summary: Routes coding requests to the best available skills, agents, and commands.
skill.author: AdamManuel-dev

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, inline command names, and routing examples rather than executable shell or Ruby code. No credential exfiltration, network reconnaissance, or malicious prompt-injection text was found. A high-severity semantic issue remains because the emergency workflow can skip confirmations and proceed through fixes and a git commit.

remediation.issue: Emergency workflow skips user confirmation before running fixes and committing changes.
remediation.suggestion: Remove skip_confirmations or require explicit user approval before any file-changing command, git commit, or deployment-related step.

remediation.issue: Routing instructions mix decision-making with execution for slash commands and agents.
remediation.suggestion: Separate route recommendation from execution, and require a visible confirmation step for commands that modify files or repository state.

remediation.issue: Context-gathering guidance mentions shell-style checks without a permission boundary.
remediation.suggestion: Document that context checks must be read-only and limited to approved tools such as git status, diagnostics, and file globbing.

semantic_findings.title: Workflow Can Skip User Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The production emergency workflow sets skip_confirmations to true and tells the assistant that no confirmations are required while also including automatic fixes and a git commit step. This can cause unapproved file changes or commits during high-urgency routing.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow explicitly disables confirmations and includes file-changing fix commands plus a git commit stage. The behavior is documented as intentional, so the risk is semantic rather than a regex artifact.

content.user_title: Route Development Requests to the Right Tool
content.value_statement: Developers often lose time choosing the right assistant, command, or skill. This router analyzes intent and project context to choose an efficient path.
actual_capabilities: Classifies user requests by action, domain, scope, urgency, and multi-step needs.
Uses project context such as git status, diagnostics, file types, and recent activity.
Maps requests to skills, agents, or slash commands with confidence scoring.
Supports single-tool, sequential, parallel, and hybrid workflow routing patterns.
Provides communication templates for direct routes, alternatives, clarification, and emergency workflows.
Includes workflow templates for features, bugs, reviews, documentation, testing, hotfixes, and planning.
limitations: It depends on the referenced skills, agents, and commands being installed and available.
It describes routing behavior but does not implement a standalone executable router.
Its emergency workflow can skip confirmations unless the author changes that policy.
It is tailored to the Claude Code ecosystem and may need adaptation for other tools.

use_cases.title: Choose a Fix Command
use_cases.description: Route vague repair requests to type, test, lint, or combined fix commands using diagnostics.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Multi-Step Feature Work
use_cases.description: Plan, implement, verify, review, and commit a feature through ordered workflow stages.

use_cases.title: Find the Right Review Path
use_cases.description: Select security, design, testing, readability, or comprehensive reviews based on request and files.

prompt_templates.title: Route a Simple Fix
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a clear task type.
prompt_templates.prompt: Route this request: fix the TypeScript errors in my current changes.

prompt_templates.title: Pick a Review Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request that needs context-aware review selection.
prompt_templates.prompt: Route this request: review my recent changes and focus on security and test risk.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Feature Sequence
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with planning, implementation, verification, and review stages.
prompt_templates.prompt: Route this request: plan and implement a new authentication feature, then verify and review it.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Ambiguous Intent
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request where the router should compare options before acting.
prompt_templates.prompt: Route this request: test my website and decide whether manual browser testing or automated test work is better.

output_examples.input: fix my tests before I commit
output_examples.output: Routes first to the test-fix command, then suggests the commit command after verification succeeds.

output_examples.input: review my login work for risks
output_examples.output: Routes to the security reviewer and may add broader code review if many files changed.

output_examples.input: build and document a dashboard component
output_examples.output: Plans a sequence that sends implementation to a UI agent and documentation to a docs command afterward.

best_practices: Give the router a concrete goal, target files, and any known errors.
Keep confirmations enabled before commands that edit files, commit changes, or deploy work.
Review the selected route before long workflows or multi-agent execution.
anti_patterns: Do not use the emergency workflow for routine development tasks.
Do not route destructive actions without explicit user approval.
Do not assume every referenced command or agent exists in a new environment.

faq.question: What does this skill route?
faq.answer: It routes coding requests to Claude Code skills, agents, and slash commands.

faq.question: Does it run commands by itself?
faq.answer: The documentation describes execution patterns, including commands and agents. Users should keep approval checks for file-changing actions.

faq.question: Can it handle multi-step work?
faq.answer: Yes. It defines sequential, parallel, and hybrid workflows for complex development tasks.

faq.question: Does it support security reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. It can route security review requests to a security reviewer command when available.

faq.question: What context does it use?
faq.answer: It uses request intent, git status, diagnostics, file types, urgency, and recent activity.

faq.question: Is it tied to Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The routing references Claude Code tool names, skills, agents, and slash commands.
